newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Malaysia says globalisation must not favour rich.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says globalisation must not favour rich.

text.p: Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad urged developing countries on Sunday to unite against a world order run by the rich while "the poor shall remain voiceless".
He called the wealthy Group of Seven (G7) industrialised states a "snooty" club, and criticised the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a conference at which he was a special guest, he said that in a global economy, national borders would be erased and competition would be fierce, but it must not favour the rich and powerful nations.

"I appreciate the genuine concern and the cooperation of many of the developed countries about developing the poor countries. But I must warn them that there will always be things they will do which will not benefit us," he said.
He cited what he called "corruption" of poorer countries with aid, forcing them to adopt positions favoured by donors.

The IMF was no different, he said. "Like the commercial banks, when they have loaded you with debt, they give you a bad credit rating and refuse you more help. And, once this happened, the World Bank insists on directing and managing your economy."
The industrialised world should help developing nations manage their economies, but poorer countries should be heard before decisions were taken on issues affecting them, he said.

"We have been totally ignored," Mahathir said. "The G7 members are snooty. They will not talk with people outside their club except Russia. In modern day liberal democracy, only the rich can have a say; the poor shall remain voiceless.
"Are we in a state to face this challenge of globalisation? Obviously not. But no one is going to wait for us to get ready, so we must face it."
The answer was a united front, he said, adding:

"The countries of southern Africa must establish contact and cooperate with the ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) member countries. Then, when faced with damaging proposals from the developed North, we can take a common stand."
